newsitem.title: USA: Insurers to pay Exxon $480 million in Valdez pact.
newsitem.headline: Insurers to pay Exxon $480 million in Valdez pact.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Thursday its insurers have agreed to pay $480 million to settle a portion of claims arising from the Exxon Valdez oil tanker spill in 1989.
The payout comes on top of an earlier $300 million partial settlement under a separate section of Exxon's general liability policy, the energy giant said.
The agreement between Exxon and its nearly 170 insurers, including certain Lloyd's of London syndicates, represents a final resolution of all matters stemming from the Valdez accident, Exxon said.
"Exxon is pleased that these claims finally have been resolved," Exxon chairman Lee R. Raymond said. "This settlement will close another chapter of this accident."

The huge claim dates back to 1989, when the Exxon Valdez oil tanker ran aground, spilling more than 260,000 barrels of crude into the Prince William Sound off Alaska, causing one of the worst oil spills in U.S. history.

For the Lloyd's insurance market, it was one of several heavy blows over the five years from 1988 to 1992 that contributed to more than 8.0 billion pounds in losses and almost led to Lloyd's bankruptcy.

After several years of bitter litigation with unhappy investors who found themselves liable for these heavy losses, Lloyd's last month completed a recovery plan to reinsure all its 1992 and prior liabilities into a new company called Equitas.

Equitas is exposed to the lion's share of the Valdez claim and its purpose is essentially to shrink, using the 14 billion pounds of assets channelled into it from the Lloyd's market and its investors to settle the liabilities.
A Lloyd's spokesman on Thursday declined to specify Equitas's share of the claim.
The international insurance market and Exxon went into mediation after a court ruling in Texas last June, which Lloyd's said it would appeal.
The insurers said Exxon was negligent in allowing Joseph Hazelwood to captain the oil tanker despite a history of drinking problems.

Thursday's settlement resolves Exxon's suit in Texas state court in Houston; an arbitration proceeding between Exxon and the insurers in New York; and a suit by the insurance underwriters against Exxon in federal district court in New York, Exxon said.
